Class OidcIssuer

java.lang.Object
iu.oidc.provider.OidcIssuer
public class OidcIssuer extends Object
This provider's own identity: what it publishes as its issuer, and the keys it signs with.

Every endpoint reads configuration through one of these rather than holding a configuration of its own, so they cannot disagree about who this provider is. The configuration arrives as a Supplier and is read on every call, so a change takes effect on the next request rather than the next deployment — a supplier over a caching configuration source is what bounds how often that read actually costs anything.

Selecting a key

A signing algorithm selects the key, and the key then determines how what it signs is signed. The two are not the same step: a client endpoint registers the algorithm an ID token issued to it must be signed with, which is what issuerKey(Algorithm) answers a key for, while signing reads the algorithm back off the key it was handed. Keeping selection here means nothing is ever signed with an algorithm no published key could verify.

    • issuerKey

      public edu.iu.crypt.WebKey issuerKey(edu.iu.crypt.WebKey.Algorithm algorithm)
      Gets a key this provider signs with.

      A key with no alg, or one whose algorithm is for encryption, is never selected: it could not sign, and the discovery document doesn't advertise it. That makes the algorithms a relying party is told about and the keys available to sign with the same set.

      Parameters:
      algorithm - required signature algorithm, or null for the first signing key configured
      Returns:
      issuer signing key
      Throws:
      IllegalStateException - if no configured key can sign with algorithm
